- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After sharp sentiment spikes (≥0.67 with +0.67+ sentiment change), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or bearish (≤0.33) and news volume is low, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model underperforms when sentiment changes abruptly downward (e.g., -0.67+ sentiment change) — adjust forecast upward by 1–4% to avoid lag.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >5% over 3 consecutive days, apply a “mean reversion” bias: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- If news volume is low (≤1.0) and sentiment is high, model overreacts — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak to avoid overcorrection.
